newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Israel's Netanyahu arrives in Moscow.
newsitem.headline: Israel's Netanyahu arrives in Moscow.

text.p: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu arrived in Moscow on Monday for talks with Russian leaders on bilateral ties and the Middle East peace process.
Netanyahu, on his first visit to Moscow since becoming prime minister nine months ago, made no comments to reporters at Moscow's Bnukovo-II airport.
Later on Monday he was expected to attend a dinner hosted by Moscow mayor Yuri Luzhkov, at the elegant Metropol hotel.
He will hold talks on Tuesday at the Kremlin with President Boris Yeltsin and is also due to meet Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin and Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov.
Netanyahu's 48-hour trip to Moscow follows a similar visit last month by Palestinian President Yasser Arafat.

Russia, co-sponsor of the 1993 Israeli-Palestinian peace accord, is keen to play a more active role in the Middle East peace process but the Israeli side is expected to lay greater emphasis on strengthening economic links.
Israel's ambassador to Russia, Aliza Shenar, told Ekho Moskvy radio in an interview on Monday that her country wanted to discuss sales of Russian gas.
Israeli officials say trade between the two countries, virtually non-existent five years ago, is now worth about $500 million a year and expanding fast.
